{{short description|Mathematician and astronomer}}
{{for|the Jewish-American civil rights activist|Florence Lewis (activist)}}
'''Florence Parthenia Lewis''' (September 24, 1877{{spnd}}March 10, 1964<ref>{{cite journal |title=Deaths |journal=The Alcalde |date=September 1964 |volume=53 |issn=1535-993X |page=45 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=QtIDAAAAMBAJ&q=Florence%20Parthenia%20Lewis%201964&pg=PA45 |access-date=December 7, 2020}}</ref>) was an American [[mathematician]] and [[astronomer]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite book|title = The Biographical Dictionary of Women in Science: L–Z|contribution-url = https://books.google.com/books?id=LTSYePZvSXYC&pg=PA782|contribution = Lewsis, Florence Parthania (1877–?)|publisher = [[Taylor & Francis]]|date = 2000-01-01|isbn = 9780415920407|language = en|first1 = Marilyn Bailey|last1 = Ogilvie|first2 = Joy Dorothy|last2 = Harvey|author-link = Marilyn Bailey Ogilvie|author2-link = Joy Harvey|pages = [https://archive.org/details/biographicaldict02ogil/page/782 782]–783|url-access = registration|url = https://archive.org/details/biographicaldict02ogil}}</ref>

== Early life and education ==
Born in [[Fort Scott, Kansas]], Lewis attended the [[University of Texas at Austin|University of Texas]] for her [[undergraduate degree]], which she received in 1897, and [[Radcliffe College]] for a [[master's degree]], which she received in 1906. She earned her [[Doctor of Philosophy|Ph.D]]. at [[Johns Hopkins University]] in [[astronomy]] and [[mathematics]].<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{cite book | title-link= Pioneering Women in American Mathematics | isbn=978-0-8218-4376-5| first1 = Judy | last1 = Green | author1-link = Judy Green (mathematician) | first2 = Jeanne | last2 = LaDuke | author2-link = Jeanne LaDuke | title=Pioneering Women in American Mathematics &mdash; The Pre-1940 PhD's | publisher=[[American Mathematical Society]], The [[London Mathematical Society]] | series=History of Mathematics | volume=34 | edition=1st | date=2008 | pages=24–25}} Biography on p.363-366 of the [https://www.ams.org/bookpages/hmath-34-PioneeringWomen.pdf Supplementary Material] at [https://www.ams.org/publications/authors/books/postpub/hmath-34 AMS]</ref>

== Career and research ==
Lewis was a professor at [[Goucher College]] for her entire teaching career, from 1908 when she was appointed as an instructor to 1938 when she retired as an emeritus professor. She was known for her studies of [[Geometry|geometrical]] interpretation of [[Invariant theory|algebraic invariants]].<ref name=":0" />

== Honors and awards ==
A longtime member of the [[American Mathematical Society]], she served on its council from 1919 to 1922. She was also a member of the [[American Astronomical Society]] and the [[Astronomical Society of the Pacific]].<ref name=":0" />
